questions.q: What economic change does the summary credit with inventing dating?
a: The Industrial Revolution drew women into cities for work
The spread of free public schooling
The invention of the automobile
The rise of social media platforms
questions.why: Lesson 1 says factory work brought men and women together away from family matchmakers.

questions.q: Before dating, who typically arranged relationships?
a: Parents and relatives acting as matchmakers
Employers and trade guilds
Teachers and local clergy
Friends and next-door neighbors
questions.why: Lesson 1 says courtship was in the hands of family before the shift to cities.

questions.q: How did shopgirls change courtship in the early 1900s?
a: They made taste and consumer style central to attraction
They introduced the concept of the blind date
They campaigned for new marriage laws
They popularized meeting at church socials
questions.why: Lesson 2 says shopgirls mimicked wealthy women, making dress and brands matter.

questions.q: What was going steady in the 1950s?
a: A dating relationship that often included physical intimacy
A formal engagement announced in church
A group outing supervised by parents
A promise to marry after finishing college
questions.why: Lesson 3 says it meant dating but usually with more than hugging and kissing.

questions.q: What point does the summary make about today's hookup culture?
a: It has roots in 1950s going steady, not a recent invention
It began with dating apps in the 2010s
It replaced marriage entirely in most countries
It started in 1920s dance halls and speakeasies
questions.why: Lesson 3 says premarital sex gained acceptance through the 1950s trend.
